current: Windshield defrosting and defogging systems on vehicles sold in Canada are regulated, requiring that every vehicle (including three-wheeled vehicles equipped with a windshield) be fitted with such a system meeting SAE Recommended Practice J902 performance standards.
proposed: Requires windshield defrosting and defogging systems, with three-wheeled vehicles covered when fitted with a windshield. Passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles must meet SAE J902 performance requirements and applicable J902 or J902a test procedures, with the modifications specified in this section.
evidence: Section 103(2) requires systems subject to 103(2.1); 103(2.1): "A three-wheeled vehicle that is equipped with a windshield shall be equipped". Section 103(3): "In the case of a passenger car or a three-wheeled vehicle" the system must meet J902 and the stated test requirements. Current summary wrongly applies the J902 performance obligation to every vehicle.

current: Section 104 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations (CMVSS 104) requires every vehicle to have a power-driven windshield wiping system with at least two speeds, one of at least 45 cycles per minute, a speed of at least 20 cycles per minute, and at least 15 cycles per minute between the highest and a lower speed. Passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles must wipe minimum percentages of areas A, B and C per SAE J903a. Every vehicle must also have a washer system meeting SAE J942.
proposed: Requires windshield wipers with at least two speeds: one at least 45 cycles/minute, a lower speed at least 20, and at least 15 between the highest and a lower speed. Passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles have minimum wiped-area requirements. Washer systems meet SAE J942 with specified modifications. Three-wheeled vehicle requirements apply when a windshield is fitted.
evidence: Sections 104(3.1) and 104(7) condition the three-wheeled vehicle wiping and washing obligations on being "equipped with a windshield". Sections 104(3), (5) and (6) set the speed, wiped area and J942 requirements. Current repeated "every vehicle" summary omits this explicit windshield condition.

current: Multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks, and buses must conform to Technical Standards Document No. 105 on Hydraulic and Electric Brake Systems.
proposed: Subject to section 135 of this Schedule, multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses must conform to TSD 105, Hydraulic and Electric Brake Systems, with the indicator-lamp and warning-statement provisions specified in this section.
evidence: Section 105(1): "Subject to section 135 of this Schedule, every multi-purpose passenger vehicle, truck and bus shall conform" to TSD 105. Current summary omits the express dependency and implies unconditional TSD105 coverage.
Section 108(1): "Every passenger car, multi-purpose passenger vehicle, truck, trailer and bus shall conform" to TSD108. Trucks have no mass cap in this clause; current tag list omits Heavy truck.

current: Mirrors installed on passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles must meet specific construction and performance requirements, including stable and adjustable mounting, unit magnification (with defined exceptions), minimum reflectance levels, and no sharp edges.
proposed: Sets mirror construction, reflectance, mounting and field-of-view requirements for passenger cars, three-wheeled vehicles, motorcycles, multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses. School buses require specified outside mirror systems. Mirror types and allowed alternatives vary by vehicle class.
evidence: Section 111(13): "Every motorcycle shall have ... mounted on each side" the specified mirrors; 111(16): "Every school bus shall have the following two outside mirror systems"; 111(26): "Every multi-purpose passenger vehicle, truck and bus, with a GVWR of 4 536 kg ... or less" has specified mirrors; 111(27) addresses heavier such vehicles. Current summary limits its stated scope to passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles.

current: Every vehicle sold or manufactured in Canada must have a unique 17-character vehicle identification number (VIN) that is permanently and indelibly marked on a structural part of the vehicle and readable without disassembly.
proposed: Requires a 17-character VIN, unique within the specified 60-year manufacturing window. It must be indelibly marked on a permitted vehicle part or permanently affixed plate or label. Specified vehicle classes must have the VIN readable through the glazing without removing parts; snowmobiles have separate marking requirements.
evidence: Section 115(1) bars reuse of VINs of model-year-1980-or-later vehicles manufactured in the preceding 60 years. Section 115(2)(b) permits structural parts, certain dashboards/dashboard covers, or separate permanently affixed plates or labels. The through-glazing/no-removal requirement is limited by 115(2)(c) to listed vehicle classes. Section 115(2.1) sets snowmobile marking rules; 115(4) requires 17 characters. Current summary incorrectly makes structural-part marking and no-disassembly readability universal.

Section 115(1): "Every vehicle shall have a vehicle identification number". Table I explicitly includes Truck (with extra data only for trucks <=4 536 kg) and Bus, as well as passenger vehicles, trailer, motorcycle and snowmobile. Current category tags omit Heavy truck and Bus.
